name: N-methyltryptamine
summary: N-Methyltryptamine (NMT), also known as monomethyltryptamine, is a chemical compound of the tryptamine family and a naturally occurring compound found in various plants and animals, including humans.

pharmacology.text: NMT is known to act as a potent serotonin 5-HT2A receptor full agonist. It has been reported to be inactive in activating the β-arrestin2 pathway of the receptor and hence appears to be a biased agonist of the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor. The drug does not seem to be an agonist of the serotonin 5-HT1A receptor. On the other hand, it is also a serotonin receptor agonist in the rat uterus and stomach strip.
pharmacology.kind: Non-selective serotonin receptor agonist; Serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist; Serotonin-releasing agent; Serotonergic psychedelic; Hallucinogen

uses.text: Orally administered NMT appears to produce no psychoactive effects, likely as a result of extensive first-pass metabolism. According to Roger W. Brimblecombe and colleagues, NMT is inactive in humans, with few details provided. On the other hand, according to reports given to Alexander Shulgin and by others, NMT is active via non-oral routes.
